articles.title: Nagaland: HC gives NHIDCL two months slope protection status on NH-29
articles.description: Morung Express NewsKohima | November 26The Gauhati High Court, Kohima Bench, has directed the National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL) to submit an updated status report on Union Road and Highway Ministry approval and the consequent tender process for slope protection measures under Packages I, II and III of the NH-29 Dimapur–Kohima four-lane project, preferably within two months. In an order dated November 25, a division bench of Justice Robin Phukan and Justice Yarenjungla Longkumer directed NHIDCL to include the updates in its affidavit, along with the status of maintenance works under Packages I and II. The State Government was also directed to submit an affidavit on pending road works and related issues. The latest directions follow the Court's November 25 review of affidavits filed by NHIDCL and the concerned contractor, detailing the progress and outstanding works across the project packages. For Package I, NHIDCL informed the Court that repair works had commenced at three of the five major identified locations. A total of 867 metres of damaged pavement across 23 locations had been identified, involving cracks, potholes, settlement, bulging and base failure. Of this, maintenance work covering 35 metres had been completed, while 832 metres remained pending. For Package II, NHIDCL stated that the tender for a short-term maintenance contract was cancelled after only one bidder participated in the second Notice Inviting Tender (NIT). The EPC contractor is currently maintaining the stretch and has completed pothole-filling works along 8.010 km on both sides of the road, it added. A lane of the National Highway 29 along the Dimapur-Kohima four-lane road at Tsiedukhru Range is seen blocked after a fresh rockfall strikes the stretch on on September 10. On November 25, the Kohima Bench, directed NHIDCL to submit, preferably within two months, an updated status report on MoRTH approval and the consequent tender process for slope protection works along the highway. (Morung File Photo) However, work along the remaining 4.725 km, from Km 138+775 to Km 143+500, remained pending due to local issues. NHIDCL informed the Court that it had sought the intervention of the Deputy Commissioner, Chumoukedima, through a letter dated November 10 to facilitate the pending works. Regarding the rockfall-prone Tsiedukhrü range, NHIDCL stated that a permanent solution involving slope protection and rockfall mitigation measures had been proposed under the Detailed Project Report (DPR), which was undergoing technical review and approval. For Package III, NHIDCL reported that major construction works had been substantially completed, with only minor rectification and balance works pending. The concerned EPC contractor had been directed to complete the remaining works, following which the process for issuance of a completion certificate would be initiated. On the slope protection measures under all three packages, NHIDCL informed the Court that the DPR consultant had submitted the final DPR on October 11. Necessary revisions were being incorporated in accordance with directions from the NHIDCL Managing Director, after which the DPR would be processed for final approval from the Ministry.NHIDCL also informed the Court that it had sought revised land rates from the DC Chumoukedima, on November 20 for land acquisition related to the slope protection works, but was yet to receive a response. The Court directed the State respondents, including the Chief Secretary, Commissioner and Secretary of PWD (Works and Housing), and Chief Engineer of PWD (National Highway), to submit an affidavit on the status of black-topping work from Lerie Welcome Gate to Jotsoma Bypass. The State was also directed to report on steps taken by the Deputy Commissioner, Kohima, regarding the Package III mudslide, with the contractor stating that the landowner was preventing debris clearance and that NHIDCL had sought the DC's intervention through a letter dated October 31. It was further asked to update the Court on land acquisition for slope protection works under all three packages. The proceedings form part of the Court's continuing monitoring of the NH-29 four-lane project through a suo motu public interest litigation instituted in 2019. The Court listed the matter for February 3, 2027, directing NHIDCL and the State respondents to file the required affidavits before the next hearing.

articles.title: Udyam Portal, Assist Platform Cross 10 Crore MSME Registrations: Govt
articles.description: Udyam Portal, Assist Platform Cross 10 Crore MSME Registrations: Govt New Delhi, Nov 26 (KNN) Registrations on the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform crossed 10 crore on October 30, 2026, marking an increase from 1.02 crore registrations in 2020, according to the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. The Udyam Registration Portal was launched on July 1, 2020, to provide enterprises with an online, paperless registration facility based on self-declaration. The system uses Aadhaar and PAN details, along with information from GST and Income Tax databases, and does not require physical document submissions or periodic renewal. Before Udyam, MSME registration was carried out through the Entrepreneurs Memorandum (EM-II) and Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM) systems. Between 2006 and September 17, 2015, around 21.96 lakh enterprises registered under EM-II through a physical application process. The UAM system, introduced on September 18, 2015, recorded around 1.02 crore registrations until June 30, 2020. The Ministry launched the Udyam Assist Platform on January 11, 2023, to facilitate the formalisation of informal micro-enterprises through designated financial institutions and partner agencies. According to the Ministry, Udyam registration enables enterprises to access various government support programmes, including the Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) and Priority Sector Lending, subject to applicable eligibility conditions. The registration framework also supports the implementation of programmes such as the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), National SC-ST Hub and Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises. Women-led enterprises accounted for 3.76 crore registrations, representing 37.8 per cent of the combined registrations on the two platforms, the Ministry said. (KNN Bureau)
